title: PMKVY 4.0 - Skill India Free Training & Certification
meta_description: PMKVY 4.0 2026 - free skill training in 200+ trades with government certification. Stipend during training, placement assistance. 1.6 crore trained since 2015.

hero.one_liner: Free skill training and certification in 200+ trades - from IT to plumbing to beauty to accounting - with stipend and placement assistance

what_is_it: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is India's flagship skill training scheme under the Skill India Mission. It provides free short-term training (200-600 hours) in over 200 trades and job roles, along with government-recognized certification, a training stipend, and placement assistance. The scheme is now in its 4th phase (PMKVY 4.0), running from 2022 to 2026.

PMKVY 4.0 focuses on new-age skills like Industry 4.0, Web 3.0, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, AR/VR, climate change solutions, and green economy jobs. As of December 2025, over 27 lakh candidates have been trained under PMKVY 4.0 across 38 sectors. Since 2015, the scheme has certified 1.29 crore candidates out of 1.64 crore trained.

Training is provided at PMKVY Training Centers (TCs) and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKKs) spread across every district in India. Courses cover sectors like IT-ITeS, retail, hospitality, healthcare, construction, automotive, beauty & wellness, agriculture, electronics, and many more. You can search training centers at pmkvyofficial.org or the Skill India Digital Hub.

After completing training and passing the assessment, candidates receive a National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) aligned certificate - recognized by employers across India. Many training centers also provide placement assistance, connecting graduates with relevant employers. Studies show that 94% of employers prefer PMKVY-trained candidates.

PMKVY also has a Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) component - if you already have skills through informal work experience (like a carpenter or tailor who learned on the job), you can get your existing skills assessed and certified without going through full training. RPL candidates receive an honorarium of ₹500 upon certification.

extra_sections.heading: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
content:
What is RPL?

Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) is a pathway for working professionals and those with informal skills to get certified without attending full training. If you've been doing a job informally for years - as a welder, plumber, tailor, or electrician - RPL lets you skip training and go straight to assessment and certification.

Who is RPL for?

RPL is ideal for workers in unregulated sectors who learned skills on the job. This includes self-employed individuals, informal workers, and those changing careers.
You must have at least basic prior experience in your chosen job role. RPL is open to candidates aged 15-45 with Aadhaar, a bank account, and relevant work experience.

How does RPL work?

The process has 4 steps: (1) Counselling & Pre-screening - you meet advisors and take a pre-screening test to confirm your skills match a job role.
(2) Orientation - 12 hours of training covering 6 hours domain knowledge, 4 hours soft skills & entrepreneurship, and 2 hours assessment familiarization.

(3) Assessment - third-party assessors test your skills across both core and non-core job competencies. (4) Certification - if you score 50% (NSQF levels 1-3) or 70% (levels 4+), you get your NSQF certificate.

What certificate do you get?

You receive an NSQF (National Skills Qualifications Framework) certificate identical to the regular PMKVY certificate. It's recognized by employers across India and is equivalent to an ITI qualification for many roles.
You also receive a marksheet, candidate payslip, and ₹500 honorarium upon certification.

extra_sections.heading: What Happens After Training
content:
Placement Rates & Job Prospects

PMKVY 4.0 does not guarantee placement, but placement assistance is provided. Training centers connect you with employers in relevant sectors.

According to earlier data (PMKVY 1.0-3.0), placement rates averaged 40-50% with significant variation by sector. IT, retail, and healthcare sectors show higher placement success (50-70%), while some construction roles have lower rates.

Certificate Value in the Job Market

Your NSQF certificate is recognized across India by both government and private employers. Studies show 94% of surveyed employers prefer PMKVY candidates.
The certificate is equivalent to ITI qualifications for many job roles. Some employers treat PMKVY graduates similarly to diploma holders depending on the sector.
Many roles in retail, hospitality, healthcare, and IT actively recruit PMKVY pass-outs.

Your Next Steps After Certification

Immediate (within 1 month): Attend placement drives organized by your training center. Update your CV with your NSQF certificate.

Register on Skill India Digital Hub for job opportunities. Reach out to industry connections suggested by your center.

Medium-term (1-3 months): If not placed, consider apprenticeships or internships in your field.

Pursue additional certifications to increase competitiveness. Use your stipend (if received) to invest in tools or further training.

Long-term (3-12 months): Explore self-employment or entrepreneurship in your field.
Consider upskilling in related areas to increase earning potential. Transition to permanent roles from temporary assignments.
Some PMKVY graduates go on to start their own businesses (plumbing, salon, repair shops, etc.).

extra_sections.heading: What is PMKVY and why it matters for unemployed youth
content: PMKVY (Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana) is India's flagship skill development scheme launched in 2015 under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. It provides free short-term skill training (2-6 months) in over 300 trades - from electrician and plumber to data entry operator and digital marketing - with a nationally recognized NSQF (National Skills Qualifications Framework) certificate upon completion.
India produces 1.5 crore graduates annually but only 20-25% are considered employable by industry standards. The gap isn't knowledge - it's practical skills.
A BCom graduate can explain accounting theory but can't operate Tally software. A BSc graduate knows physics equations but can't wire an electrical panel.
PMKVY bridges this employability gap by training youth in job-ready skills that employers actually demand.

The scheme is now in its third phase (PMKVY 3.0/4.0) with a target of training 1 crore youth across India. Training is conducted at PMKVY Training Centres (TCs) - typically private institutes that are accredited by NSDC (National Skill Development Corporation) and affiliated with Sector Skill Councils.
You don't pay for the training - the government pays the training centre directly.

extra_sections.heading: What courses are available?
content: IT and Digital: Data Entry Operator, Computer Hardware & Networking, Web Developer, Digital Marketing Executive, Cyber Security Analyst, Medical Transcriptionist. These courses last 2-4 months and lead to immediate employment in BPOs, IT companies, hospitals, and digital marketing agencies.
Starting salary: Rs 10,000-18,000/month.

Construction and Infrastructure: Electrician, Plumber, Mason, Painter, Welder, Carpenter, Bar Bender, Crane Operator. These trades have massive demand in India's construction boom - metro projects, highways, smart cities, real estate development.
Starting salary: Rs 12,000-25,000/month. Experienced tradespeople earn Rs 30,000-50,000/month.
Healthcare: General Duty Assistant (GDA), Home Health Aide, Phlebotomist, Emergency Medical Technician, Medical Lab Technician Assistant. Post-COVID, healthcare skill demand has exploded.
GDA courses lead to hospital employment within 1 month of completion. Starting salary: Rs 10,000-15,000/month in hospitals.
Beauty and Wellness: Beauty Therapist, Hair Stylist, Spa Therapist, Nail Art Technician, Makeup Artist. Booming sector - India's beauty industry grows at 15-20% annually.
PMKVY-certified beauticians get placement in salon chains (Lakme, VLCC, Naturals) or start their own business with Mudra loan. Starting salary: Rs 8,000-15,000/month (much higher in metros).
Automotive: Motor Vehicle Mechanic, Auto Electrician, EV Service Technician, Auto Body Painter, Two-Wheeler Service Technician. With 25 crore vehicles on Indian roads, mechanic demand is permanent.
EV service technician is a new high-demand trade - Ola, Ather, TVS, and Tata EV owners need specialized service. Starting salary: Rs 10,000-20,000/month.

extra_sections.heading: How to enroll in PMKVY - step by step
content: Step 1: Visit skillindia.nsdcindia.org or the Skill India Digital Hub (SID) portal. Browse available courses by sector, location, and duration.
Filter by your district to find training centres near you. Each listing shows the trade name, duration, training centre address, batch start date, and placement support details.
Step 2: Register on the portal with your Aadhaar, mobile number, and basic educational details. Select the course and training centre you want.
You may need to visit the training centre for a brief assessment (basic aptitude test) before enrollment is confirmed. This assessment ensures you're placed in the right skill level.
Step 3: Attend the training. Courses run 4-8 hours daily for 2-6 months depending on the trade.
Training includes theory (20-30%), practical/hands-on (60-70%), and soft skills (10% - communication, workplace behavior, interview preparation). Attendance requirement: 80% minimum.
Below 80% attendance disqualifies you from certification and reward money.

Step 4: After training, take the assessment exam conducted by the respective Sector Skill Council. The assessment is practical + theory - you demonstrate your skills to an external assessor (not your trainer).
If you pass, you receive the NSQF-aligned certificate and the reward money (Rs 500/month during training + Rs 8,000 on successful assessment).

Step 5: Placement support. The training centre is required to provide placement assistance - connecting you with employers, organizing campus interviews, and sharing your profile with placement agencies.
The government tracks placement rates and penalizes training centres with low placement. Ask about the centre's placement track record before enrolling.

extra_sections.heading: Financial benefits - you get PAID to learn skills
content: Training stipend: Rs 500/month during the training period (credited to your bank account via DBT). For a 4-month course: Rs 2,000 total stipend. This small amount covers your daily transport to the training centre.

Reward on completion: Rs 8,000 (approximate - varies by course) credited to your bank account after you pass the assessment and receive the certificate. This is the government's incentive for completing the course - many trainees drop out midway, so the reward encourages completion.

Free training worth Rs 15,000-50,000: The actual cost of the training (instructor salary, equipment, materials, venue) is Rs 15,000-50,000 depending on the trade. The government pays this directly to the training centre.
You receive this training at zero cost. If you had to pay for the same course at a private institute, you'd spend Rs 20,000-1,00,000.

Total financial value: Free training (Rs 15,000-50,000 value) + stipend (Rs 2,000-3,000) + reward (Rs 8,000) + placement support + nationally recognized certificate. All for zero investment from your side.
The only 'cost' is your time - 2-6 months of attending daily training. For an unemployed youth, this is the highest-ROI investment available.

extra_sections.heading: PMKVY certificate - where is it recognized?
content: The PMKVY certificate is aligned with NSQF (National Skills Qualifications Framework) - India's national competency framework for vocational skills. It's recognized by all government departments, public sector companies, and most private employers across India.
The certificate has a QR code that employers can scan to verify authenticity.

Government job relevance: Several government recruitments accept NSQF/PMKVY certificates as skill qualification - ITI-equivalent for some Group C positions, preferred qualification for multi-tasking staff in government offices, and eligibility criteria for some state government contractual positions. Check specific recruitment notifications for NSQF recognition.

International recognition: PMKVY certificates for certain trades (welding, nursing assistance, plumbing) are mapped to international standards - enabling migration for employment to Gulf countries, Singapore, and other destinations that accept Indian skill certifications. The Pravasi Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PKVY) specifically trains PMKVY graduates for overseas employment.

Employer acceptance: Major employers that actively hire PMKVY graduates: Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors, Wipro, Infosys BPO, Apollo Hospitals, Fortis Healthcare, Lakme, VLCC, L&T, Godrej, Dabur, and hundreds of MSMEs. The NSDC maintains a placement portal where certified graduates are matched with employers seeking specific skills.

extra_sections.heading: How to choose the right PMKVY course
content: Match your interest and aptitude: Don't choose a course just because your friend is doing it. If you enjoy working with your hands, choose trades like electrician, plumber, or mechanic.
If you prefer computers, choose data entry, web development, or digital marketing. If you enjoy interacting with people, choose beauty therapy, retail sales, or healthcare assistance.

Check local job demand: A web developer course is great in Noida but less useful in a village in Bundelkhand where there are no IT companies. A tractor mechanic course is excellent in agricultural areas but less relevant in Bangalore.
Research which skills have demand in YOUR area - talk to local employers, visit job sites (Naukri, Indeed), and ask the training centre about their placement locations.
Verify the training centre's quality: Not all PMKVY training centres are equal. Some are excellent with industry-standard equipment and experienced trainers.

Others are poorly equipped classrooms with theoretical-only teaching. Before enrolling: visit the centre in person, check the equipment and labs, ask current trainees about their experience, and verify the centre's NSDC accreditation at nsdcindia.org.
Consider career progression: Some PMKVY courses are standalone (beauty therapy - you can start working immediately). Others are stepping stones (GDA → nursing diploma → BSc Nursing).
Choose courses that open career pathways, not dead ends. A PMKVY electrician certificate + 2 years of work experience qualifies you for supervisor roles earning Rs 30,000-40,000/month.

extra_sections.heading: Complete the course - Rs 8,000 reward + certificate only for finishers
extra_sections.content: 40% of PMKVY trainees drop out before completing the course - losing the certificate, reward money, and placement support. The most common reason: 'I got a daily wage job and stopped attending training.' That daily wage job pays Rs 300-500/day today. The PMKVY certificate qualifies you for Rs 500-800/day jobs permanently. Don't sacrifice long-term career growth for short-term daily wages.

extra_sections.heading: Verify the training centre is NSDC-accredited
extra_sections.content: Some fake institutes advertise 'PMKVY training' but are not accredited by NSDC. Their certificates are worthless. Before enrolling, verify the centre at nsdcindia.org → Training Partner Directory. The centre should have a valid TP (Training Partner) code. If the centre isn't listed, it's not legitimate - walk away and find an accredited centre nearby.

extra_sections.text: 1.4 crore youth trained. 300+ trades. Zero cost to the trainee. Free nationally recognized certificate + Rs 8,000 reward + placement support. PMKVY is the largest free skill training program in the world. If you're unemployed and have 2-6 months to invest, there is no better use of your time than a PMKVY course.

extra_sections.heading: PMKVY Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) - for experienced workers
content: Already have skills from years of work experience but no formal certificate? PMKVY's RPL (Recognition of Prior Learning) component is specifically for you.

RPL assesses and certifies existing skills of experienced workers - without requiring them to undergo full-length training. A carpenter with 10 years of experience gets his skills formally assessed and receives the same NSQF certificate as a fresh PMKVY trainee.
RPL process: Register through the PMKVY portal or visit an RPL assessment centre. Complete a brief bridge training (12-80 hours depending on the trade - much shorter than the full 2-6 month course).
Take the assessment conducted by the Sector Skill Council. If you pass, receive the NSQF certificate + Rs 500 reward.
The entire process takes 1-2 weeks.

Why RPL matters: India has 30+ crore informal workers with genuine skills but no paper qualification. A plumber who has been fixing pipes for 15 years is more skilled than a fresh PMKVY trainee - but without a certificate, he can't apply for government contractor panels, large construction company positions, or overseas employment.
RPL gives him the paper credential that his skills deserve.

RPL at your workplace: NSDC can organize RPL assessment camps at factories, construction sites, and industrial areas - so workers don't need to take leave. Employers benefit too - a workforce with formal certifications improves the company's compliance ratings and project bidding eligibility.
Ask your employer to arrange an RPL camp or contact your nearest PMKVY training centre.

extra_sections.heading: PMKVY vs ITI vs polytechnic - which skill path to choose
content: PMKVY: Short-term (2-6 months), free, 300+ trades, basic to intermediate skill level, suitable for quick employment. Best for: unemployed youth who need a job within 6 months, school dropouts (8th-10th pass accepted for many trades), and workers seeking formal certification of existing skills (RPL).
Limitation: the certificate is recognized but carries less weight than ITI for government job applications.

ITI (Industrial Training Institute): Long-term (1-2 years), nominal fee (Rs 1,000-5,000/year in government ITIs), 130+ trades, intermediate to advanced skill level. ITI certificate is equivalent to Class 10 board exam for government job eligibility.
Best for: 10th pass students who want a comprehensive trade qualification. ITI graduates earn Rs 12,000-25,000/month starting, rising to Rs 30,000-50,000 with experience.
Polytechnic Diploma: 3 years after 10th, covers engineering trades at diploma level. Graduates can work as junior engineers, site supervisors, and technicians.
Polytechnic diploma holders are eligible for government technical posts (JE, technician grades). Starting salary: Rs 15,000-30,000/month.
Best for: students who want engineering-adjacent careers without a 4-year BTech degree.

Sequential strategy: Do PMKVY first (2-6 months, free) → get employed → join ITI part-time/evening if your trade requires deeper skills → eventually pursue polytechnic diploma if you want supervisory roles. Each level builds on the previous one.
PMKVY is the fastest entry point - don't skip it in favor of waiting 2 years for ITI admission.

extra_sections.heading: Success stories and placement data
content: PMKVY has trained over 1.4 crore youth since 2015. Aggregate placement rate is approximately 50-55% - meaning roughly half of certified graduates find employment within 3 months of completion.
The other half either pursue further education, start self-employment, or face local job market constraints. IT and healthcare sectors have the highest placement rates (60-70%).

The scheme has been particularly impactful for women. 52% of PMKVY trainees are women - and beauty, healthcare, retail, and apparel trades have 60%+ female enrollment. A woman from a rural area who completes a PMKVY beautician course and joins a Lakme salon in a nearby town earning Rs 12,000/month represents genuine economic empowerment that a degree alone doesn't provide.

Criticism: Some training centres focus on enrollment numbers rather than quality - training 200 students with 5 computers doesn't produce employable graduates. NSDC has tightened quality monitoring with surprise inspections, trainee feedback systems, and performance-linked payments to training centres.
Before enrolling, check the centre's NSDC rating and ask recent graduates about their experience.

extra_sections.description: 300+ courses from IT to healthcare available at 15,000+ training centers.

how_to_apply.title: Visit pmkvyofficial.org or Skill India Digital portal
how_to_apply.description: Search for training centers near you. Filter by sector, job role, and location. You can also call the helpline at 088000-55555 for assistance in finding centers.

how_to_apply.title: Visit the training center and enroll
how_to_apply.description: Carry Aadhaar card, educational certificates, bank passbook, and passport photos. The center will verify your eligibility and enroll you. No fee is charged for registration.

how_to_apply.title: Complete training and pass assessment
how_to_apply.description: Attend classes regularly (usually 2-6 months depending on course). After completion, take the assessment conducted by a third-party agency approved by Sector Skill Councils. Pass marks are 50% for NSQF levels 1-3 and 70% for level 4+.

how_to_apply.title: Get placement assistance and start career
how_to_apply.description: Training centers connect you with employers through placement drives and interviews. Your NSQF certificate and digital profile on Skill India are your credentials. Centers may also provide entrepreneurship guidance if you prefer self-employment.

important_alert.text: PMKVY training is 100% FREE. If any center asks for money for training, assessment, or certification, it's unauthorized. Report immediately at the helpline 088000-55555 or at pmkvyofficial.org. Only ₹500 candidate honorarium (for RPL) is government-provided cash.

important_dates.label: Enrollment
important_dates.value: Open throughout the year - rolling admissions

faqs.question: Will I get a job after PMKVY training?
faqs.answer: PMKVY provides placement ASSISTANCE, not guaranteed placement. Training centers connect you with employers in the relevant sector. Placement rates vary by sector and location - IT, retail, and healthcare have higher rates (50-70%). The NSQF certificate significantly improves your employability compared to having no certification. Studies show 94% of employers prefer PMKVY candidates.

faqs.question: I'm 35 and already working. Can I join?
faqs.answer: Yes. PMKVY is open up to age 45. If you want to upskill or learn a new trade, you're eligible. The Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) component is specifically designed for working adults - get your existing skills certified without leaving your job.

faqs.question: Is the PMKVY certificate recognized by private companies?
faqs.answer: Yes. The NSQF (National Skills Qualifications Framework) certificate is recognized across India by both government and private employers. It's aligned with industry standards and is equivalent to an ITI certificate for many job roles.

faqs.question: Can I do PMKVY twice in different sectors?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can enroll in multiple PMKVY courses in different sectors across your lifetime. However, each course must be completed separately with its own assessment. Some centers may have specific policies - check with your local training center for details.

faqs.question: Is online training available under PMKVY?
faqs.answer: PMKVY 4.0 emphasizes in-person practical training since most skills require hands-on learning. However, the Skill India Digital Hub provides online modules for orientation, soft skills, and theory components. Practical training and assessments must be completed at registered training centers.

faqs.question: How do I verify if a training center is genuine?
faqs.answer: Visit pmkvyofficial.org and search for registered centers in your location. Genuine centers will have government recognition displayed. Your center should have proper facilities, qualified instructors, and be registered with Sector Skill Councils. If unsure, call the helpline 088000-55555 to verify the center's authenticity.

faqs.question: What's the difference between PMKVY and ITI?
faqs.answer: ITIs provide longer training (6 months to 3 years) in 126 trades with a 70% theory, 30% practical mix. PMKVY offers shorter, focused training (2-6 months) in 200+ trades with 70% practical, 30% theory focus. PMKVY is faster and more employment-focused; ITI is more comprehensive. ITI graduates report ~63.5% placement rates; PMKVY candidates have showed higher employer preference (94%). Choose PMKVY for quick upskilling, ITI for deeper technical knowledge.

faqs.question: Do I need a bank account to enroll in PMKVY?
faqs.answer: Yes, you'll need an active bank account (preferably linked to Aadhaar) for receiving stipends, candidate honorarium, and placements. You can open a basic savings account at any bank free of cost.

faqs.question: Is PMKVY training really free?
faqs.answer: Yes - 100% free for the trainee. The government pays the training centre Rs 15,000-50,000 per trainee directly. You pay nothing - no registration fee, no tuition fee, no exam fee, no hidden charges. If any centre asks you for money, it's a violation - report to the NSDC helpline at 088000 55555 or email pmkvy@nsdcindia.org.

faqs.question: What is the age limit for PMKVY?
faqs.answer: 15-45 years for most courses. Some specialized courses have narrower age ranges. There's no formal educational qualification required for many trades - even 8th pass or 10th pass candidates can enroll for trades like mason, painter, tailor, cook. For IT courses, 12th pass is typically required.

faqs.question: Will I get a job after PMKVY training?
faqs.answer: The training centre provides placement ASSISTANCE - not guaranteed placement. Placement rates vary: IT courses have 60-70% placement, healthcare 50-60%, beauty 40-50%, construction trades 70-80% (highest demand). Your placement depends on your skill level, attendance, assessment score, and local job market. Centres with strong industry connections have better placement rates.

faqs.question: Can I do PMKVY along with college?
faqs.answer: Yes - many PMKVY courses have flexible timings (evening batches, weekend batches) that don't conflict with college schedules. A BCom student can do a PMKVY Tally + GST Accounting course in evenings. A BSc student can do a PMKVY Lab Technician course on weekends. The skill certificate complements your degree and makes you more employable than degree-only graduates.
